title: Correct the VTT product-vision document: the world is genuinely free-camera 3D, not 2.5D; 2.5D is demoted to an optional per-asset representation technique for tokens/items
objective: Owner-directed correction: docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md's Product Vision section currently states the VTT targets a '2.5D look' achieved via a fixed isometric-ish camera (the TaleSpire framing). The owner explicitly rejected this: the world (terrain, buildings, environment) must support a genuinely free 3D camera -- top-down, side-on, orbit, any angle, no fixed/locked presentation. 2.5D is not discarded entirely, but rescoped to an optional representation technique for specific asset classes only (tokens/characters, some items) that may render as flat/billboarded 2D art standing inside the fully 3D environment, analogous to tabletop-miniature standees or billboarded sprites in a 3D world (Doom-style billboarding, Octopath Traveler's HD-2D). This does not change the already-Decided rendering architecture (Three.js remains the sole renderer for both views) -- free camera navigation and sprite billboarding are both native, ordinary Three.js capabilities (OrbitControls-style free camera, THREE.Sprite for billboards), so no dependency or architecture decision is affected, only the product-vision narrative and its downstream implications for asset-authoring guidance.
validations: Corrected the 'Product vision' section's opening paragraph and 'Key clarification' paragraph: removed the claim that the VTT targets a scene-wide 2.5D look via a fixed isometric-ish camera; replaced with a correction stating the environment (terrain/buildings/scene) is genuinely free 3D with an unrestricted camera, and 2.5D is rescoped to an optional per-asset representation technique (tokens/items only), noting THREE.Sprite billboarding as the native Three.js mechanism for that technique.
Confirmed via grep that '2.5D' only appeared in this one document, contained to the Product Vision section (lines ~20-35) -- no other research document or registry entry needed correction.

No change to the already-Decided rendering-architecture table (Three.js sole renderer for both views) -- free camera and billboarding are both ordinary Three.js capabilities, not a new dependency or architectural fork.
No dependency installed, no code written, no ADR reopened -- documentation correction only.

Checked docs/research/RESEARCH-DECISIONS-REGISTRY.md per the PostToolUse research-registry-reminder hook: grepped for '2.5D'/'isometric'/'camera', no matches -- the registry only tracks tool/candidate adoption status (Adopted/Standby/Discarded/Reference only), and no candidate's status changed by this correction (Three.js remains the sole Decided renderer), so no registry edit was needed.
risks: Documentation-only correction -- no code, no dependency, no ADR change.

Downstream sections of the same document (guided construction mode, reference-game table, etc.) were written assuming a free-3D world already (they describe full terrain relief, orbit-relevant techniques like InstancedMesh hexagons, Raycaster-based editing) and do not need further correction from this change -- verified by re-reading the full document before editing.
